reconcile.note: Gill attributes Mary's failure to recognize Jesus in John to tears, shock, and no expectation of seeing him alive, not a real conflict with Matthew's joy.

discrepancy.note: Strauss reads John's Mary Magdalene as failing to recognize the risen Jesus at all, unlike Matthew's joyful, immediately recognizing women.

quotes.text: she however, does not recognize him even when he speaks to her, but takes him for the gardener, until he (in the tone so familiar to her) calls her by her name.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), §139, on John 20:14.

sides.verseText: They departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to bring his disciples word.

sides.snippet: didn't know that it was Jesus
sides.verseText: When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing, and didn't know that it was Jesus.
